statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-14661, the sslkeylogfile connection parameter letting a user of dblink or CREATE/ALTER SUBSCRIPTION append data to a file of their choosing, in 17.12. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-14661/ lists 17.12 as the fixed release for major version 17 and says versions before 18 are affected when libpq 18 or later is installed and in use by the server; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-14661. dblink.so, postgres_fdw.so and libpqwalreceiver.so (used by subscriptions) are in the postgresql-17 package of every published build on amd64 and arm64 and link libpq.so.5. The libpq5 package published from this source in the DHI Debian repository is built from PostgreSQL 17, and the 17.11-1 and 17.12-0 packages carry their own libpq.so.5.17 from the same release, so these builds do not ship libpq 18; because a server can be run against a libpq 18 installed from elsewhere, the builds before 17.12 are still recorded as affected, following upstream's table. The postgres server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix, and 17.12-0 is the lowest published build that does. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
